Decades and parts of a period
Place events in a decade or part of a period.

В шестидесятых годах — in the 1960s. В девяностых годах — in the 1990s. These expressions refer to decade ranges rather than a single year. The ordinal describing the decade and the noun meaning years are in the prepositional plural.

For these examples, assume the twentieth century. A decade expression by itself does not fix the century in every context; an explicit century or the surrounding discussion can identify it.

В конце года — at the end of the year. В начале века — at the beginning of the century. The position word identifies which part of the period is meant, while the following noun identifies the period. Both parts matter: an end is not a beginning, and a year is not a century.

In these expressions, the location noun after the preposition is prepositional, and the noun naming the period is genitive. The English of relationship links the part to the larger period. Do not assign one case to both nouns simply because they appear in the same time phrase.

В середине недели — in the middle of the week. This locates an event within the central part of a week; it does not mean the end of a year or the beginning of a century.
Distinguish when something happens from the interval over which it happens.

Она родилась во время войны. — She was born during the war. Во время поездки я познакомился с новыми друзьями. — During the trip I met new friends. The war and trip are the surrounding events during which the birth and meeting happen. During does not mean that the birth or meeting continued for the entire war or trip.

The compound preposition meaning during takes the event noun in the genitive. Match the whole sentence: birth during a war differs from meeting friends during a trip. This expresses when an event happens within another event, not the time needed to complete a task. For the time phrase meaning during the war, write во время войны.

В течение урока ученики работали над проектом. — Throughout the lesson, the students worked on the project. В течение дня погода менялась несколько раз. — During the course of the day, the weather changed several times. The interval contains the activity or repeated events. Project work over the lesson does not by itself assert that the project was finished.

It emphasizes the duration over which something occurs. The compound preposition takes a genitive noun naming the interval. The weather example explicitly describes several changes during the day, so the expression need not mean one continuous unchanged action. Compare the whole proposition as well as the interval: students and a project differ from weather changes.
Before, after, in a year and a year ago
Place an event relative to another event or time.

Перед ужином мы ходили в парк. — before. После работы я смотрела фильм. — after. The first places the park visit earlier than dinner; the second places watching a film later than work. The preposition meaning before takes an instrumental noun; the one meaning after takes a genitive noun.

The future-looking in expression locates an event after an interval from the reference time. Ago locates an event before the reference time. Neither meaning alone states how long the activity lasts or how long it takes to finish a task. Before and after a named event likewise express order relative to that event, not completion.

Мы едем в Латвию через год. — in (a period of time). Мы ездили в Казахстан год назад. — ago. In the first sentence the planned Latvia journey is a year after the reference time; in the second the Kazakhstan journey was a year before it. The forward-looking time construction takes accusative, not genitive; the time noun here has the same surface form as nominative. In the example, the time span comes before the word for ago.
